To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) s-wave reduced neutron width distributions of the Pt isotopes 192,194 exhibit anomalous fluctuations; (ii) the anomalous fluctuations are not due to a statistical fluctuation; (iii) the Porter-Thomas (PT) distribution is ruled out as the underlying statistical distribution; (iv) the PT distribution, which is a member of the gamma distribution family, is rejected by our data at the 99.997% confidence level.
the s-wave neutron widths of 1.8 MeV resonances of 192,193,194Pt do not follow the Porter-Thomas statistics and that the reduced widths of these resonances are strongly correlated with each other.

1) the s-wave reduced neutron width distributions of 192, 194Pt are not described by the Porter-Thomas distributions and 2) the s-wave neutron width distributions of these nuclei have a non-zero mean and variance that are significantly smaller than predicted by the Porter- Thomas distributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the anomalous behavior of reduced neutron widths of s-wave resonances in the region of 192, 194Pt.
the study of nuclear level spacings, and their fluctuations, in the neutron-rich nuclei 192,194Pd, 192,194Os and 192,194Ir.
the anomalous fluctuations of the s-wave reduced neutron width of 192, 194 Pt resonances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed deviations from the Porter-Thomas (P-T) distribution are not statistically significant.
the s-wave reduced neutron width distributions for 192,194 Pt are anomalous and cannot be described by a Porter-Thomas distribution.
the Porter-Thomas hypothesis is not supported by the data, and that the observed fluctuations of reduced neutron widths are anomalous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the s-wave reduced neutron width distribution of 192, 194Pt has a long tail.
the s-wave reduced widths are not distributed as a Porter-Thomas distribution but rather as an exponential distribution.
the Porter-Thomas hypothesis is rejected in the energy region from 1.5 eV up to the neutron binding energy of the target.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Porter-Thomas (PT) distribution is not valid for s-wave neutron widths.
s-wave reduced neutron width distributions are not Porter-Thomas distributed.
a new statistical distribution is needed to describe the s-wave neutron widths.
